Tian Rui teased her that a notebook could not prepare primary routes by staring at its owner from the pillow. Yue left it on the table and read something ordinary before bed. Tian's son had learned the sentence he struggled with and now repeated it at every meal, to everyone's mild exasperation. Their room life held small changes independent of Yue's examination ambition. She could be proud of an actual recovered practice and still want a quiet supper without discussing it again.

lantern_15_062.speaker: narrator
lantern_15_062.text: Shao closed the course record and asked what ordinary livelihood would support the next interval. Yue's school post ended on Day 1628. Pu had an ordinary workshop inventory and public safety-sheet job running Day 1629 through Day 1650, twenty-two calendar days at four copper each. It involved two-hour duty mornings, accepted rest dates, and no live personal operation. Its eighty-eight copper came from the workshop's existing received maintenance-documentation allocation. The source was Pu's business, not the river-hall reserve. Yue read the actual demands before accepting the term, with enough ordinary time for later preparation.

lantern_15_063.speaker: narrator
lantern_15_063.text: Fang's second ordinary courier acknowledgment arrived before his final departure. The two-day outward route had held, its local receiving task was completed, and the paid return ended on Day 1628. The third departure would leave the following morning, outside Yue's completed school term. She helped the class find its actual public date on the notice before returning the teaching materials to He Pu. The lesson ended with a service still ahead rather than a fictional acknowledgment copied in advance. Children could plan from a real future booking without treating it as a completed event.

lantern_15_064.speaker: narrator
lantern_15_064.text: The school's final batch was accepted on Day 1628 and paid forty-five copper, the remaining fifteen calendar days at three. Yue's completed thirty-nine-day term now totaled one hundred seventeen actually received. He Pu retained the school materials and thanked her for the layout and route corrections. He offered no indefinite unpaid obligation to keep future sheets current. A later public teaching post remained a possible separately funded relationship whose actual invitation had not arrived. Yue returned the school key, kept her own received work record and public sheets, and went home for supper before the next employer's morning.

lantern_15_065.speaker: narrator
lantern_15_065.text: He Pu's farewell to Yue's finite post was a ordinary lunch after its final received batch. Tian Rui had accepted a later copying order of her own and described the particular page she hoped would not contain another crossed-out word. Yue laughed and handed her the public editing note they were permitted to share. She did not keep the school originals to remain involved after her key was returned. The work had ended; the people could still meet. A later invitation would become a new term only if its dates, pay, and actual receiver were agreed.

lantern_15_066.speaker: narrator
lantern_15_066.text: Yue went to bed early before Pu's new workshop morning. Her four-cell block was spent, her current ordinary following condition was normal, and the stage-nine threshold remained unearned. The room held received wages, a few chosen public pages, and letters whose private owners had permitted particular readings. It did not contain the entire town's archive or a missing certificate waiting to be named. She turned down the ordinary lamp, listened to the upstairs child finally stop repeating his sentence, and slept. The next day had work of its own, which would matter before any later title did.
